title: Failed sends retry on their own

why.quote: When a send fails I only find out hours later.
Nobody should have to press send twice.

change.before: A failed send stays failed until someone notices and presses send again.
change.after: A failed send retries on its own, and the user sees when it gave up.

mustHold: A message is never sent twice.
Retries stop after the configured limit.

problem.evidence: The user described the missed sends in their own words.

goals.evidence: Retry and give-up are both observable in the outbox.

criteria.evidence: Both checks name a command or a reviewer.

scope.evidence: Backoff tuning is out; the retry worker is in.

consistency.evidence: The worker and the outbox read the same attempt count.

claims.text: A failed send retries three times, five minutes apart.

decision.question: How many retries before the worker stops?

options.label: None. The user presses Try again

decision.reason: Three covers a brief outage without hiding a real failure.

rejected.reason: It is the problem we are fixing.

children.text: The worker reads the attempt count before each send.
The attempt count lives on the outbox row.

claims.text: The outbox shows when a send gave up.

decision.question: What does a given-up send say?
decision.reason: The count tells the user retries already happened.

rejected.reason: Reads as if nothing was tried.

decision.question: Where does the setting live?
decision.reason: Config already holds the outbox settings.

checks.criterion: A given-up send is easy to spot

check.judgment: Look at the outbox with one given-up send

units.title: Retry worker
units.goal: Retry failed sends up to the limit.

units.title: Gave-up label
units.goal: Show when a send gave up.
units.design: Adds one label; removing it restores the old row.

dropped: A retry button on every row
